content.title: About
content.content: French toast sticks are fried bread strips coated in a mixture of eggs, milk, cinnamon and sugar. Served hot, they are often accompanied by maple syrup, fruit sauce or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The stick form became popular in the US in the 1970s as a convenient fast‑food version of classic French toast.
They are a common breakfast‑on‑the‑go item in fast‑food chains and coffee shops.
The cinnamon‑sugar coating gives them the familiar aroma of traditional French toast in a portable shape.
Some restaurants serve them with ice cream, creating a "French toast sundae".
A vegan version can be made by replacing eggs with a plant‑based substitute.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter provide a modest amount of complete protein useful for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk adds calcium, which supports bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and whole‑grain bread supply B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from cinnamon
items.content: Cinnamon contains polyphenols that may help reduce inflammation.

items.title: Balanced sugar when prepared wisely
items.content: Using moderate sugar and pairing with berries can make the dish more nutritionally balanced.

items.title: High sugar and fat content
items.content: Frying in oil and adding sugar increases calories and can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs or lactose should use alternative ingredients.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten; gluten‑free bread can be used for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Burn hazard during frying
items.content: Hot oil can cause burns, so cooking should be done with care.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sticks hot, drizzled with maple syrup, fruit coulis, chocolate ganache, or simply dusted with powdered sugar. They are easy to eat with hands as a snack or as part of a breakfast platter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat briefly in a skillet or microwave before serving.
